sections.heading: C — Signs, Signals and Markings
sections.markdown:
## C — Signs, Signals and Markings

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Signs tell road, system, flow, and local rules, warn of hazards, mark routes, and set speed and movement, from big green overhead interstate panels to small blue library and hospital rectangles, and fixed shape-and-color meanings let drivers read them at once, so a battered red octagon still orders a stop while any rectangle always regulates law and instruction with speed caps as its example [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Red-octagon stop signs demand a full halt before the crosswalk whether marked or not with waiting until every direction clears, a red rectangle reading four-way or all-way under a stop sign stops all approaches, red-and-white yield triangles order slowing with readiness to halt and granting oncoming traffic first, and a red ring slashed through means do-not or not-allowed [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Red covers stop, yield, and prohibition, orange covers construction and maintenance warning, yellow covers general warning, fluorescent yellow-green highlights schools, pedestrians, and bicyclists, white and black set rules and instructions, green guides, blue serves drivers, and brown marks recreation, culture, and history [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
State law under Title forty-seven, section eleven-two hundred seven makes blocking or harming roads, traffic devices, sign boards, guide signs, or posts a misdemeanor, and when the act injures or kills anyone the responsible people face felony guilt with up to two years of imprisonment plus a one-thousand-dollar fine or both [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A02
Black-and-white rectangular regulatory signs command what drivers must and must not do, control traffic for safety, bind exactly like other traffic laws, order school-zone slowing to the posted cap under a flashing yellow with watching for children and readiness to halt, and reserve marked disabled spaces for plated or placarded vehicles only [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A02
Lane-use panels may send one lane left while its neighbor chooses left or straight, or pin one lane straight while its neighbor chooses right or straight, other rectangles ban left turns, all turns, U-turns, right turns, trucks, or bicycles, order keeping right of objects or dividers, use the center lane for left turns only with no passing, forbid entry to oncoming one-way roadways, cap speed at the posted maximum for ideal conditions, and bar passing across yellow lines where sight distance falls short [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A03
Diamond yellow-background black-letter warning signs announce hazards, direction shifts, and nearby activity ahead and demand extra care, covering signals ahead, divided highway starts and ends, gentle curves, narrow bridges and culverts, merges, added lanes needing no merge, steep hills, clearance limits, school zones and crossings, deer and pedestrian crossings with yielding, stop signs ahead, ending right lanes, and two-way traffic with right-lane driving [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A04
Roadside object reflectors flag culverts, piers, rails, obstructions, and alignment at night, pass-to-side panels and barricade stripes point where traffic must go with downward-right stripes bearing right and downward-left bearing left, and T-intersection signs force a right or left turn with yielding [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A04
Round yellow-and-black advance signs and black-and-white crossbucks announce rails ahead with slowing and readiness to halt fifteen to fifty feet short of the first track, crawling when views block until tracks show, stopping for any visible train, halting school buses, church buses, motor coaches, and explosives or flammable haulers by law, forbidding passing of such halted vehicles except on multi-lane highways, and yielding to oncoming trains after looking and listening with track-count plates at multi-track crossings [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A05
Flashing crossbuck lights mean a train approaches and order stopping until it passes with every track confirmed clear, gated crossings order halting when lights start before the gate falls and waiting until gates rise and lights die, and quiet zones silence routine horns behind No Train Horn signs with engineers still free to sound for emergencies while zone crossings may add local safety measures [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A05
Orange marks work zones with mostly diamond and some rectangular signs plus cones, barrels, and barricades guiding drivers and shielding crews, hazardous sites demand slowing to the posted cap with doubled speeding fines where workers or equipment stand, drivers must slow or stop, shift lanes, follow orders, and react fast, and flashing arrow panels assign the proper lane [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A06
Orange-hatted orange-clad flagpersons with red signs or flags control extreme hazards and the law demands obedience, ordered halts happen in-lane without swerving with no advance until waved on, drivers proceed warily past crews and machines watching for opposing traffic, conviction for ignoring work signs brings a misdemeanor of one hundred to one thousand dollars plus up to thirty days in jail with property and injury liability, and speeding fines double where workers or equipment stand [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A06
Cones, drums, and barricade panels channel traffic flow, and the slow-moving-vehicle emblem marks farm, construction, and maintenance rigs crawling public highways at twenty-five miles per hour or less [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A07
Green, white, or brown guide signs give travel facts on highways, distances, exits, and parks, business-route guides follow numbered highways into commercial districts, mileposts flag crash and breakdown spots each interstate mile from the state line with north-south counting from the south and east-west from the west, overhead green interstate arrows assign lanes, blue service signs point at fuel, food, and lodging, and litter barrels at rest areas, picnic grounds, and toll stations with a posted hotline are the only lawful highway trash drops [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A08
Traffic signals grant right-of-way by direction and bind all drivers unless an officer directs otherwise, green permits crossing or lawful turns after checking the intersection clear, steady yellow warns of coming red and orders halting when safely possible with smooth slowing and no racing, red orders a full pre-crosswalk halt held until green, stopped drivers may then turn right on red or left from one-way into one-way absent bans while yielding to every intersection user including bicycles, and green arrows permit only the arrowed turn even under red with turning-only lanes waiting for the arrow from the proper lane plus yielding to crosswalk pedestrians and lawful traffic [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A08
Flashing yellow arrows allow cautious left turns after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians who keep priority, flashing red equals a stop sign at risky crossings with proceeding only when safe, flashing red arrows ban all arrowed turns until green, flashing yellow orders slow careful passage with both-direction looks and halt readiness, drivers still yield on green whenever yielding averts a crash even when wronged, and color-blind drivers read position with red top, yellow middle, and green bottom [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A09
Pedestrian signals alone govern foot and wheelchair crossings over vehicle signals, steady figures release the curb, flashing figures hold starters back while letting crossers finish, and red figures bar leaving the curb, while lane-control signals close lanes on red, warn clearing on yellow with flashing yellow permitting left turns, and open lanes on green, and yellow-and-white pavement stripes assign lanes, flag blind passing bans, reveal opposing next-lane traffic, and mark left-turn waiting spots with broken yellow allowing passing, solid yellow in your lane forbidding it, double solid banning both directions except left-turn center crossing, and single solid freeing only the broken side [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0027]
